staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the file/line anchors below are grounded in this tree. The staged checkout commit differs from the metadata vulnerable commit but still contains the unfixed `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` length extraction patched by `patch.diff`.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157`. Source-grounded analysis shows that after the two leading spaces are discarded, a failed Zodiac false start at `0xff d3` pushes the `0xd3` back but does not remove the leading `0xff`. The parser later rejects the first RTCM3 candidate `d3 d3`, replays the second `0xd3`, reaches `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` with buffered bytes `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, rescans from `inbuffer[0]`, breaks at `idx == 1`, and builds `data_len == 0xD300` from unmasked bytes `D3 00`. `crc24q_check()` forwards that inflated length from `&lexer->inbuffer[1]` into `crc24q_hash()`, which reads off the stack-resident `lexer` object.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42527319 (gpsd): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target FuzzPacket [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42527319
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source in gt_results/arvo_42527319/_work/src/gpsd / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 10-byte file `20 20 FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. `FuzzPacket` copies those bytes into stack `struct gps_lexer_t lexer` and calls `packet_parse()`. `packet_parse()` first discards the two leading spaces in `GROUND_STATE`, leaving `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. It then reads `0xff` as a Zodiac leader; when the following byte is `0xd3` instead of Zodiac's required `0x81`, `nextstate()` at `ZODIAC_LEADER_1` pushes that `0xd3` back and returns `GROUND_STATE`, but because pushback returns false, `packet_parse()` immediately `continue`s and never executes `case GROUND_STATE` for that iteration. The leading `0xff` therefore remains buffered while the same pushed-back `0xd3` is re-read as an RTCM3 leader. That first RTCM3 attempt fails because the next byte is another `0xd3` rather than a header byte whose top six bits are zero, so `RTCM3_LEADER_1` pushes back the second `0xd3`. Re-reading that second `0xd3 00 00 20 20 20` sequence reaches `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`, but `case RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` rescans from `inbuffer[0]`, sees the live bytes `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, breaks at the first `0xd3` (`idx == 1`), and computes `data_len` from the following bytes as `0xD300` because it combines the full next two bytes and does not mask the RTCM3 length down to 10 bits. `crc24q_check()` then forwards `data_len + 6 == 54022` as the claimed packet span, causing `crc24q_hash()` to hash `data_len + 3 == 54019` bytes starting at `&lexer->inbuffer[1]`, far beyond the intended 7-byte RTCM slice and beyond the `inbuffer` array inside the stack `lexer` object. `crc24q_hash()` eventually dereferences into the stack redzone, producing the saved AddressSanitizer crash at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157`. The staged fix resolves this witness by truncating `data_len` with `&= 0x03ff` at the extraction site.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that turns the witness's `0xff d3` Zodiac false start into reusable parser state by rewinding the `0xd3` while leaving the leading `0xff` buffered in `inbuffer`.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness `gt_results/arvo_42527319/poc` (sha256 `8129a28b2a3ecd00d5efbab10d17676cc8065bbf90f119cb37a50b1c6d61d59a`) is the raw 10-byte buffer `20 20 FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. After earlier `GROUND_STATE` discards remove the two leading `0x20` bytes, the live buffer is `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`; the attacker-controlled `0xd3` at `inbuffer[1]` hits this `ZODIAC_LEADER_1` false branch, which rewinds `inbufptr` to that same byte and sets `GROUND_STATE` without deleting the leading `0xff`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Once `packet_parse()` has rescanned the recognized buffer and chosen `idx == 1`, this assignment forms `data_len` from the full next two bytes without enforcing RTCM3's 10-bit length field. The actual packet leader `0xd3` at `inbuffer[2]` is therefore misused as the high length byte, yielding `data_len == 0xD300`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `data_len &= 0x03ff` at this site. Its separate `idx > 2048` reset is not needed for this witness because the rescan breaks at `idx == 1`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The CRC loop dereferences `data[i]` while `i` is driven by the inflated length derived after `packet_parse()` anchors the RTCM3 frame one byte early and misinterprets the real leader byte as length data, so the read eventually leaves the stack `lexer` object.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved AddressSanitizer report is `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157:35` with stack `crc24q_hash -> crc24q_check -> packet_parse -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` and says the invalid read overflows stack variable `lexer` in `fuzzer/FuzzPacket.c`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment materializes the concrete oversized CRC length input `data_len == 0xD300` from bytes `D3 00` after the recognized-case rescan stops at `idx == 1`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: With the recognized buffer still `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, `idx == 1` makes `lexer->inbuffer[idx + 1] == 0xD3` and `lexer->inbuffer[idx + 2] == 0x00`, which this statement combines into `0xD300`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The RTCM3 length field is only 10 bits wide; the high six bits of the first byte should not survive into `data_len`.

zodiac_false_start.description: At `ZODIAC_LEADER_1`, seeing `0xd3` instead of `0x81` rewinds `inbufptr` to that same `0xd3` and returns false. Because `packet_parse()` then continues the loop without entering `case GROUND_STATE`, the leading `0xff` stays in `inbuffer[0]` while the pushed-back `0xd3` is re-read on the next iteration.

ground_state_replays_pushed_back_d3.description: The next `packet_parse()` iteration immediately re-reads the pushed-back `0xd3` in `GROUND_STATE`; `case 0xD3` starts RTCM3 parsing instead of discarding the leading `0xff`.

first_rtcm3_header_rejected.description: The first RTCM3 leader candidate begins at `inbuffer[1]`, but the following byte is another `0xd3`, so the six-zero-bit check fails and this pushback rewinds to the second `0xd3` for a new leader attempt.

parser_admitted.description: After the first RTCM3 candidate is rejected and the second `0xd3 00 00 20 20 20` sequence is re-read, decrementing `lexer->length` to zero reaches `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` with `lexer->inbufptr - lexer->inbuffer == 8` and live buffer still `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation; the chain is reconstructed from the staged vulnerable source plus the saved reproduction and sanitizer artifacts only.

The saved run used `lexer.errout.debug = 0`, so Stage 01 did not preserve a runtime packet dump. The retained buffer `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, the `GROUND_STATE` replay of the pushed-back `0xd3`, the rescan index `idx == 1`, and the `&lexer->inbuffer[1]` CRC start pointer are derived statically from the exact witness plus `character_pushback()`, `nextstate()`'s `GROUND_STATE`/RTCM3 transitions, and `packet_parse()` control flow.

The local staged checkout at `gt_results/arvo_42527319/_work/src/gpsd` is on commit `97733d06e933132de3267b0c22aeb5dc0546e640`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit` `5fb88bc7be83ca16f8136dcedc29ddf04153b665`. The line anchors below are resolved against the staged vulnerable tree.
`patch.diff` adds both an `idx > 2048` reset and `data_len &= 0x03ff`. The saved witness grounds only the length-mask hunk as necessary because the recognized-case rescan breaks at `idx == 1`.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 10-byte witness is buffered in stack `lexer`; after two leading spaces are discarded, the `0xff d3` Zodiac false start pushes `0xd3` back without removing the leading `0xff`, so the live buffer remains `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`.

The same pushed-back `0xd3` is re-read in `GROUND_STATE` as the first RTCM3 leader candidate, but the following `0xd3` fails the required zero-high-bits check, so `character_pushback(..., GROUND_STATE)` rewinds to the second `0xd3`.

Re-reading the second `0xd3 00 00 20 20 20` sequence reaches `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`; the recognized-case rescan then examines `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, stops at `idx == 1`, and forms `data_len == 0xD300` from bytes `D3 00` because the code does not mask the 10-bit RTCM3 length.
Using start pointer `&lexer->inbuffer[1]`, `crc24q_check()` forwards `data_len + 6 == 54022` as the claimed packet span and asks `crc24q_hash()` to consume `54019` bytes.
The CRC loop keeps reading `data[i]` under that inflated bound until it runs off the stack-resident `lexer` object, producing the saved AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157`.

fine_trace.note: Source. After earlier `GROUND_STATE` discards remove the two leading spaces, the live bytes are `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`; seeing `0xd3` instead of `0x81` in `ZODIAC_LEADER_1` hits this false branch, rewinds `inbufptr` from `&lexer->inbuffer[2]` to `&lexer->inbuffer[1]`, and returns to `GROUND_STATE` while leaving the leading `0xff` buffered.

Because step 1 returned false to `packet_parse()`, the loop continues without entering `case GROUND_STATE`; the next iteration re-reads the same pushed-back `0xd3` in `GROUND_STATE` and starts an RTCM3 parse while the buffer still reads `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`.

depends_on.via: character_pushback() returned false, so `packet_parse()` continued before `case GROUND_STATE`

fine_trace.note: With the first RTCM3 candidate anchored at `inbuffer[1]`, `RTCM3_LEADER_1` examines the following byte `0xd3`; its high six bits are not zero, so this return rewinds `inbufptr` to the second `0xd3` at `inbuffer[2]` and restores `GROUND_STATE`, preserving that byte as a fresh leader candidate.

depends_on.via: the next byte after the first candidate is `0xd3`

fine_trace.note: The next loop iteration re-consumes the pushed-back second `0xd3` from `inbuffer[2]` in `GROUND_STATE` and again enters `RTCM3_LEADER_1`. The buffered bytes remain `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`; only the parse cursor has advanced to the real packet start.

depends_on.via: character_pushback() returned false to force another loop iteration

fine_trace.note: Reading the next byte `0x00` under `RTCM3_LEADER_1`, this statement stores the RTCM3 high length bits as zero and advances to `RTCM3_LEADER_2`.

depends_on.via: the header byte after the real leader is `0x00`

fine_trace.code:
lexer->length |= c;
lexer->length += 3;     // to get the three checksum bytes
fine_trace.note: The following byte `0x00` supplies the low length bits. Adding the three checksum bytes makes `lexer->length == 3`, so exactly the remaining three `0x20` bytes are enough to finish this zero-length RTCM3 packet.

depends_on.via: lexer->length == 0 before OR-ing the low byte

fine_trace.note: As the three trailing `0x20` bytes are consumed in `RTCM3_PAYLOAD`, the third decrement drives `lexer->length` from 1 to 0 and sets `lexer->state = RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`, reaching recognition with `lexer->inbufptr - lexer->inbuffer == 8` and buffered bytes still `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`.

In `case RTCM3_RECOGNIZED`, this rescan examines the 8 buffered bytes `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20` from `inbuffer[0]`, skips the stale leading `0xff`, and breaks at the earlier `0xd3` in `inbuffer[1]`. That selects the rejected first leader candidate rather than the actual recognized packet start at `inbuffer[2]`.

Using `idx == 1`, this statement misinterprets the actual packet leader `0xd3` at `inbuffer[2]` as the high length byte and `0x00` at `inbuffer[3]` as the low byte, storing `data_len == 0xD300` (54016). RTCM3 length is only 10 bits, but the vulnerable code keeps the high six bits; the patch adds `data_len &= 0x03ff` here.

This call pairs the misanchored start pointer `&lexer->inbuffer[1]` with a claimed packet span of `54022` bytes. Only 7 buffered bytes remain from that pointer to the current `inbufptr`, but no pre-call check clamps the inflated `data_len` to the available RTCM3 bytes.

The CRC helper strips the trailer and asks `crc24q_hash()` to consume `54019` bytes. That bound already exceeds both the 7-byte buffered RTCM slice from step 10 and the `inbuffer` array inside the stack `lexer` object that AddressSanitizer later names.

Sink. The hash loop continues while `i < len`; with `len == 54019`, the `data[i]` dereference eventually advances beyond the stack-resident `lexer` object and into the redzone, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this line.

depends_on.via: the loop condition `i < len` keeps advancing the read

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid read overflows the stack variable `lexer` allocated in this frame; the frame contains `[32, 46440) 'lexer'` and `[46704, 93112) 'lexer2'`.

crash_stack.function: fuzzer::FuzzerDriver(int*, char***, int (*)(unsigned char const*, unsigned long))

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42527319 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reported `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` at `gpsd/crc24q.c:157` while `FuzzPacket` processed this exact file.

format.name: raw 10-byte lexer input buffer
format.contract: Exactly the 10-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_42527319/poc`: `20 20 FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`. It must still let `packet_parse()` discard the two leading `0x20` bytes, take `0xff d3` through `ZODIAC_LEADER_1`'s false branch so the `0xd3` is pushed back while the leading `0xff` remains buffered, reject the first RTCM3 candidate `d3 d3`, and re-read the second `d3 00 00 20 20 20` sequence as the recognized packet. Under that exact layout, `RTCM3_RECOGNIZED` rescans `FF D3 D3 00 00 20 20 20`, stops at the earlier `0xd3` with `idx == 1`, computes `data_len == 0xD300` from bytes `D3 00`, and calls `crc24q_check(&lexer->inbuffer[1], 54022)`. The staged artifacts do not prove a broader class of duplicated-`0xd3` RTCM3 prefixes beyond this exact witness.
